findings.conditions: updatefaceElemMatrix: a faster rank leaves the function and sends its next message on mpiComm_ (any tag) before this owner has finished its receive loop; or a message from another phase is still in flight
findings.reasoning: The owner of a shared face receives with MPI_ANY_SOURCE and MPI_ANY_TAG on mpiComm_ and treats Status.MPI_TAG as a face global ID. Nothing synchronises at the end of the function: the Isends are never waited on and there is no barrier. A rank that has finished can go on to later communication on the same communicator (for example the 33420/33421 messages of updateNodeElemMatrix, or the next call), and this wildcard receive can take that message. The BinarySearch of an unrelated tag then returns -1, so cols[-1] and ncols[-1] are read and written (memory corruption or a crash). Otherwise a foreign payload of up to 100 ints is appended to some face. The real face message is left unmatched, and later receives see an off-by-one stream. Even with no foreign message, the order in which columns are appended depends on arrival order.

findings.conditions: ParaSailsSetupPatternExt: a fast rank finishes ExchangePrunedRowsExt and issues its ExchangePrunedRowsExt2 requests (same tag ROW_PRUNED_REQ_TAG) while a slower rank is still in Ext's last ReceiveRequest loop and a request from a third rank is still in transit
findings.reasoning: ReceiveRequest probes MPI_ANY_SOURCE on ROW_PRUNED_REQ_TAG, and Ext and Ext2 use the same tag with nothing to synchronise them. The FindNumReplies Allreduce comes after each phase's Isends, so P can be in Ext2 and have sent its request to Q while R's Ext request to Q is still in flight. Q's Ext loop then takes P's Ext2 request and answers it from pruned_rows_local. Its Ext2 loop later takes R's Ext request and answers it from pruned_rows_global. The counts still balance, so nothing hangs, but P and R merge pruned rows built with the wrong threshold. The pattern of the preconditioner, and the result, then differ between runs. The same cross-level matching inside the level loops is harmless, because there the reply data is the same.

findings.conditions: MPI_Send not buffered (rendezvous or zero-buffer semantics) and a cyclic or symmetric neighbour pattern (P sends lengths to Q while Q sends to P)
findings.reasoning: In HYPRE_LSI_MLConstructMHMatrix every rank first runs blocking MPI_Send of the length message (tag 539) to all of its recvProc. Only afterwards does it post MPI_Recv(MPI_ANY_SOURCE, 539). No receive is pre-posted. With a symmetric off-processor coupling (the usual case), two neighbours each block in MPI_Send waiting for the other to receive, so the program deadlocks unless the implementation buffers the send eagerly. Later phases pre-post Irecv, but this one does not.

findings.conditions: MPI_Send not buffered and neighbours that send to each other
findings.reasoning: Same pattern as HYPRE_LSI_ml.c: blocking MPI_Send of recvLeng (msgid 539) to every recvProc, then MPI_Recv(MPI_ANY_SOURCE, 539) for sendProcCnt messages, with no receive pre-posted. Whether it completes depends on eager buffering. Under zero-buffer semantics, two ranks that need data from each other deadlock in MPI_Send.

findings.conditions: Two hypre_LocateAssumedPartition calls on the same communicator with no intervening synchronisation; a fast rank's tag-17 message from the second call reaches a slow rank still waiting in the first
findings.reasoning: The receive loop takes MPI_ANY_SOURCE messages with a fixed tag 17 until rows_found == locate_row_count. Nothing ties a message to one invocation. A rank that has finished the first call can send its range for the next partition (another matrix or vector) to a rank still in the first loop. That message is counted against the wrong partition, so proc_list and the row ranges are wrong. rows_found can also overshoot locate_row_count, and then the != test never becomes true and the rank blocks forever. The real message is left for the next call.
